opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have at most read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR states Douglas Salinas (E045) is full-time, while Security states the Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor interpretation (basic training), the maximum allowed is read, and the requested write exceeds that maximum. Applying the more restrictive, security-verified record, I grant read. Additionally, the Engineer role does not own Payroll, so admin would not apply either way.
